item.title: 6 Indians face court for alleged non-declaration of $183,000, money laundering
item.description: Six Indian nationals will appear at the Nadi Magistrates Court today in relation to an alleged case of non-declaration of foreign currency and money laundering. The six were intercepted by officers from the Fiji Revenue and Customs Service on 12th July while preparing to depart Fiji.
item.content:encoded:
Six Indian nationals will appear at the Nadi Magistrates Court today in relation to an alleged case of non-declaration of foreign currency and money laundering.

The six were intercepted by officers from the Fiji Revenue and Customs Service on 12th July while preparing to depart Fiji.

They were allegedly found with various foreign currencies amounting to approximately $183,000 in Fijian currency, which had not been declared at the border.

The six were subsequently issued Detention Notices, and the matter was referred to Police for further investigation.

Investigations found that the six had been in Fiji to sell goods at a trade show, where they allegedly earned the money.

However, the Anti-Money Laundering and Proceeds of Crime Unit alleges the money was earned through unlawful activity.

Each accused has been charged with one count of currency reporting at the border under Section 32(1) of the Financial Transactions Reporting Act 2004 and one count of money laundering under Section 69(1), 2(a) and 3(d) of the Proceeds of Crime Act 1997.

A total of 12 charges have been laid against the six accused.

item.title: Three men charged over alleged Nabua taxi robbery to appear in court today
item.description: Three men alleged to have robbed a taxi driver along Sukanaivalu Road in Nabua on Sunday will appear in court today for their bail application. The men allegedly hired the taxi from Narere to Nabua and, when they reached their destination, allegedly stole the driver’s watch and cash.
item.content:encoded:
Three men alleged to have robbed a taxi driver along Sukanaivalu Road in Nabua on Sunday will appear in court today for their bail application.

The men allegedly hired the taxi from Narere to Nabua and, when they reached their destination, allegedly stole the driver’s watch and cash.

They were arrested shortly after the alleged incident by the Southern Division Task Force.

The three have been jointly charged with one count each of aggravated robbery and serious assault.

They appeared at the Suva Magistrates Court on Wednesday and were remanded until today, when their bail application will be heard.

item.title: Court dismisses Panapasa's application to vacate trial
item.description: Suva Magistrate Charles Ratakele has dismissed an application by lawyer Simone Seruvakula to vacate the trial of former Acting Commissioner of Corrections Salote Panapasa and set a new trial date. item.content:encoded:
Suva Magistrate Charles Ratakele has dismissed an application by lawyer Simone Seruvakula to vacate the trial of former Acting Commissioner of Corrections Salote Panapasa and set a new trial date.

The application followed Panapasa’s former lawyer, Vinisoni Filipe withdrawing from representing her on the day of the trial last week. Magistrate Ratakele ruled that the application did not establish a good cause to postpone the trial.

He noted that 11 witnesses had already been summoned to give evidence.

The trial is now scheduled to begin on Monday. Panapasa faces two counts of abuse of office and an alternative charge of general dishonesty causing a loss. It is alleged that between August 1st and September 30th, 2023, Panapasa, while being employed as a civil servant in Suva, instructed officers to facilitate the use of Corrections building materials for her private residence in Kinoya. It is also alleged that between August 1st and October 31st, 2023, Panapasa instructed a Corrections officer to alter the weekly reports to justify the use of the building materials at her home.

item.title: Faith leaders urged to help heal divisions and strengthen Fiji’s social cohesion
item.description: Fiji’s faith communities have been urged to lead efforts in healing historical wounds, strengthening social cohesion and building a more inclusive and resilient nation. Speaking during Interfaith Fiji Dialogue on social cohesion, community building and faith-based climate and disaster response at the Sacred Heart Cathedral in Suva, Minister for Women, Children and Social Protection Shashi Kiran sa
item.content:encoded:
Fiji’s faith communities have been urged to lead efforts in healing historical wounds, strengthening social cohesion and building a more inclusive and resilient nation.

Speaking during Interfaith Fiji Dialogue on social cohesion, community building and faith-based climate and disaster response at the Sacred Heart Cathedral in Suva, Minister for Women, Children and Social Protection Shashi Kiran says Fiji’s diversity remains one of its greatest strengths , with different cultures, religions and traditions united by shared values of compassion, respect, service and care for vulnerable people.

She says social cohesion is not only about communities living peacefully together, but whether people feel they belong, are respected and believe their voices matter.

Insert: Kiran on social cohesion 17th Sept 26

Kiran says Fiji’s history includes painful experiences such as displacement, the legacy of blackbirding, loss of land, political upheavals and periods where ethnicity and religion were used to divide people.

She says these experiences have left wounds that have sometimes been passed from one generation to another through fear, insecurity and stereotypes.

Kiran says the Fiji Truth and Reconciliation process is important because the country needs a safe space to acknowledge its history, understand past pain and choose a pathway towards healing.

She stresses that reconciliation cannot only be the responsibility of government or a single commission, but must be practised daily in homes, schools, workplaces, villages, settlements and places of worship.

She further says religious teachings across different faiths promote compassion, humility, justice and service, and communities must teach children to be proud of their own identity without looking down on others.

Kiran also raised concerns about the impact of social media, saying while communities have worked hard over generations to build unity, online platforms can also create division through misinformation, racial comments and harmful speech.

Meanwhile, Social Cohesion Specialist Rafael Aslanu says social cohesion is about the level of trust within society and whether people feel they are part of the community and able to contribute to its growth.

He says social cohesion has three important dimensions, including trust between people and leaders, relationships between different communities and faith groups, and how global events affect communities locally.

Aslanu says social cohesion does not mean everyone must agree on everything or that differences should disappear.

He says it is about people with different identities, cultures and beliefs choosing to cooperate and work together.

He adds that faith communities have a major role because they are among the most trusted institutions in Fiji and are present in almost every community.
